item.title: The Reader: A new review source for book lovers
item.description: Most newspapers and wire services have closed the book on sections devoted to book reviews. But Washington Monthly's new online resource, The Reader (co-founded by bestselling author Jonathan Alter), offers book reviews, essays, and recommendations by some of the world's top writers. Jane Pauley reports.

item.description: Korean-American novelist Min Jin Lee, bestselling author of "Pachinko," talks with correspondent Jo Ling Kent about her latest book, "American Hagwon," part of her series chronicling the migration of Koreans around the world.

item.title: U2 on 50 years and their duet with Dolly Parton
item.description: The Irish quartet celebrates its 50th birthday with "Carnaval de Luz," their first album of new music in nearly nine years. Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. talk about their song "Torn," a duet with Dolly Parton that would prove to be her last recording.

item.title: U2 on 50 years and their duet with Dolly Parton
item.description: The Irish quartet U2 is celebrating its 50th birthday with "Carnaval de Luz," their first album of new music in nearly nine years. Bandmembers Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. talk with correspondent Anthony Mason about revisiting the Dublin school where they first came together; regrouping following Mullen's neck surgery; and the song "Torn," a duet with Dolly Parton that would prove to be her last recording.

item.title: Disney animation legend Floyd Norman on a lifetime of make-believe and mischief
item.description: For 70 years, Floyd Norman brought drawings to life, animating some of Disney's most beloved stories, like "The Jungle Book" and "Mulan." And even after he was asked to retire, the first Black animator at Disney kept showing up at the office, mentoring and advising young animators. Correspondent Faith Salie talks with Norman (honored this weekend with a lifetime achievement Oscar) about a career marked by optimism, magic, and a wicked sense of humor.

item.title: Flights expected to normalize by tonight after ground stop. Here's what to know
item.description: Officials attributed the ground stop to aging system infrastructure and legacy technology.

item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade turns 100
item.description: This year, Macy's celebrates its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City. Correspondent Mo Rocca learns how, a century ago, puppeteer and artist Tony Sarg created the parade's iconic balloons, floats and costumes. Rocca also visits the Macy's Studio in Moonachie, N.J., where preparations for this year's parade are being designed, painted and inflated.

item.title: Aiding veterans with the healing arts
item.description: With her in-person and virtual painting workshops and online tutorials, artist Mary Whyte teaches veterans to use art to deal with isolation and trauma through her "watercolor boot camps." Correspondent Martha Teichner reports on an arts program, now in 48 states, that helps veterans' self-expression, and allows them to reconnect with fellow vets, their communities – and themselves.

item.title: "November 1963": Did the mob kill JFK?
item.description: A new film posits that the Kennedy assassination was tied to a Chicago crime boss, Sam Giancana. Screenwriter Nicki Celozzi, actor John Travolta, and Giancana's daughter, Bonnie, discuss the mob's alleged connection to a murder that changed the world.

item.title: "November 1963": Did the mob kill JFK?
item.description: A new film, "November 1963," posits that the assassination of President John F. Kennedy was tied to a Chicago crime syndicate and its boss, Sam Giancana. Correspondent Lee Cowan talks with screenwriter Nicki Celozzi – Giancana's great-nephew – along with star John Travolta and Giancana's daughter, Bonnie, about the mob's alleged connection to a murder that changed the world.

item.title: U.S. reportedly floated trading Ukrainian land for NATO membership
item.description: The Ukrainian president said he would put the question of a potential exchange to the people if certain guarantees were in place.

item.title: UPS plane, passenger jet collide on Miami airport taxiway
item.description: A UPS cargo plane and a Copa Airlines jet carrying 172 people collided while taxiing at Miami International Airport, leaving two passengers with minor injuries.

item.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian strikes, Tehran targets U.S. assets
item.description: The attacks come after the U.S. carried out minor strikes on Iran's Qeshm island in recent weeks.
